items.reason: Passing raw guests instead of uniqueGuests misclassifies existing attendees and sends them scheduled emails.
EventManager uses the requesting user's credentials instead of the organizer's, preventing correct calendar updates.
The comment includes the unbounded guest-array problem and resulting email fanout, explicitly proposing a server-side count limit.
The permission check uses && instead of ||, wrongly rejecting team admins who are not owners.
The comment includes the blacklist bypass caused by comparing unnormalized guest emails against lowercased blacklist entries.
Different casing in a submitted guest email bypasses the lowercased blacklist.
The Remove email tooltip is hard-coded English instead of using a translation key.
Using && for the admin/owner check wrongly denies team admins who are not owners.
Guest emails are not lowercased before comparison with the blacklist, allowing case-variant bypasses.
The always-truthy template string makes the generic error fallback unreachable and can display an undefined code prefix.

This concerns exposing arbitrary backend error details without checking for a known translation key. Fixing the always-truthy fallback in issue #13 would not prevent disclosure of nonempty backend error messages.
The comment includes the same case-sensitive blacklist bypass, alongside case-sensitive attendee deduplication.
The template string is always truthy, making the fallback dead code and allowing an undefined code prefix.
It repeats the claim that calendar-update failure escapes after persistence, skips emails, and makes retries fail as duplicates.
Concurrent requests can both pass the stale attendee check and insert the same email because the read and insertion lack an atomic uniqueness guard.
The comment includes the blacklist bypass from unnormalized guest emails, with additional detail about case-variant attendee duplicates.
Passing raw guests to the email sender treats resubmitted existing attendees as newly added and sends the wrong notification.
The email sender receives raw guests instead of the inserted uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees to receive AttendeeScheduledEmail.
